b1_effectiveBudget.status: FIXED AND OBSERVED ON THE ACTUAL SERVICE
b1_effectiveBudget.defect: the page was trimmed only against the 64 KiB transport cap, so a 2048-byte request could return a whole page far above it; the earlier small-page harness had copied the pager logic and therefore could not see this
b1_effectiveBudget.fix: the encoded page is trimmed against the EFFECTIVE requested budget (min(requested, inline limit)), falling back to the empty-envelope size only when even the envelope exceeds it
b1_effectiveBudget.harness: tests/native-acceptance/b28-budget.mjs (spawns the real runner-service with its own FileCriticalJournal and measures the bytes actually received)
cases: B28-ACTUAL-SERVICE-2048-BOUND - the real service returned 979 bytes for a 2048-byte request (1 frame, next 1, done false)
B28-ACTUAL-SERVICE-16384-BOUND - 2998 bytes for a 16384-byte request (3 frames)
B28-ACTUAL-SERVICE-CONTINUITY - walked the real journal over small pages with contiguous seq and no duplicates
B28-ACTUAL-SERVICE-REFUSALS - invalid cursor and out-of-range budgets (1 and 999999999) refused as invalid_since / invalid_page_budget instead of being clamped
b1_effectiveBudget.limit: the fixture lane produced only 3 real journal facts, so the 160-small-record continuity is still only observed at the helper level (wave-27 b27-small-pages), not on the actual service
